title: refactor(ci): simplify lint/test workflows, consolidate release automation, bump actions & deps
author: Jordan Li
description: Motivation: our GitHub Actions workflows have proliferated over time (lint/test/release split across multiple files), which makes caching, action pinning, and maintenance harder. This PR consolidates the lint and test workflows into a single, cache-friendly pipeline, standardizes action versions across workflows, updates several Actions and Node toolchains, and simplifies release automation to reduce flakiness observed in release previews. Changes are intentionally conservative: no functional change to product code, only CI/infra and dev tooling. Scope: - Merge lint and test job matrices into .github/workflows/ci.yml for faster incremental execution and shared caching. - Introduce a shared actions/common.yml composite for reusable steps (checkout, setup-node, restore-cache, upload-cache, install-deps, run-tests). - Pin GH Actions versions to specific minor commits where available, and bump official actions to recommended versions (actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4). - Bump Node.js build matrix to node 18 LTS for build/test jobs while keeping node 20 in release and canary where required. - Consolidate release automation into .github/workflows/release.yml: use same semantic-release configuration and add a dry-run step for release-preview. - Add repository-level cache keys based on lockfile hash and project path to reduce cache misses across monorepo packages. - Add basic CI hygiene checks: workflow linting, action-version audit, and remove deprecated workflows. Checklist: - [x] consolidate lint & unit test jobs - [x] add shared composite actions - [x] pin and bump GH actions versions - [x] add cache key improvements - [x] update release pipeline dry-run and preview step - [x] run CI and fix flakiness reported in canary runs How to review: focus on workflow files in .github/workflows/ and the new scripts/ci/* helpers. This PR intentionally keeps the change set small in source files and concentrates on CI logic. Related: ENG-2345 (CI reliability), ENG-2390 (release automation flakiness).

review_comments: Priya Natarajan: Thanks for the cleanup — overall looks great. A few nits: can we avoid mixing node 18 in test matrix and node 20 in release? It makes reproducing failures harder. Suggest keeping node 18/20 in both until we fully validate.
Jordan Li: Good point. I switched the CI matrix to test against node 18 and 20 for the next two weeks, and left release workflow anchored to node 20. Will monitor and revert if we see regressions.
Ethan Marsh: release dry-run is helpful. Can we also add an explicit semantic-release config check to the hygiene workflow?
Jordan Li: Added sanity check in hygiene.yml to run node tools/ci/semantic-release-config.js --dry-run. See last commit.
Carlos Vega: cache key suggestion: include project path and package-lock hash. Done in scripts/ci/cache-keys.sh — looks good.
Priya Natarajan: Approving with comment: please watch the first week of release previews; revert action pin if we hit infra-side flakiness.
Ethan Marsh: CI passed on the last run (unit/e2e/lint). LGTM.

merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash. Author ran a final CI and release dry-run before merging.
release_notes: Consolidated CI workflows for lint & tests, pinned and bumped GitHub Actions, improved cache keys to reduce CI startup time, added release preview dry-run and hygiene checks. No product code changes.
notes_for_ops: Monitor first two release cycles for any semantic-release regressions; observe cache hit rates and CI wall-clock time. If release-preview flakiness appears, revert action pins to prior major versions.
revert_plan: If breakage found: 1) revert this PR branch; 2) reintroduce prior workflow files and re-pin known-good action versions; 3) rollback release-preview runs and rerun semantic-release dry-run. Keep rollback PR small and targeted.
notes: Small follow-ups tracked separately: - Split shared composite into smaller steps if runtime increases; - Add matrix filtering per package for monorepo in a follow-up PR.
